**Name of the Surah**

• It is called al-Qiyamah (the Resurrection), because it opens with God's oath by the Day of Resurrection, to magnify it and affirm that it will certainly occur.

**From the Objectives of the Surah**

• Affirming the resurrection by swearing to its occurrence, and establishing the gathering and the return (to God) through rational proofs and demonstrations; reminding of the Day of Resurrection, mentioning some of its signs that point to its terror; alluding to the division of creation on that Day into the blessed and the wretched, mentioning the description of each group; and explaining the condition of the human being at the time of death and the anguish that accompanies it.

• Directing the Prophet ﷺ to the manner in which he should be when receiving the Qur'an from Jibril (Gabriel).

**[The Tafsir]**

God, glorified is He, swears by the Day of Reckoning and recompense, and swears by the believing, God-fearing soul that blames its owner for abandoning acts of obedience and committing grave sins, that the people will surely be resurrected. Does this human being, the disbeliever, think that We will not be able to gather his bones after they have been scattered? Yes indeed, We will gather them, being capable of making his fingers, or his fingertips, after gathering and reassembling them, into a perfectly formed creation, just as they were before death.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 75, verse 16–19:

Do not move your tongue, O Prophet, with the Qur'an when the revelation descends, so that you may hasten to memorize it, fearing that it will slip away from you. Indeed, upon Us is its collection in your breast and its recitation by your tongue whenever you wish. So when Our messenger Jibril recites it to you, listen to his recitation and be attentive to it. Then recite it as he has taught you to recite it. Then, indeed, upon Us is its clarification of what has become unclear to you in its meanings and its rulings.

The matter is not as you claim, O assembly of polytheists, that there is no resurrection and no recompense. Rather, you are a people who love this world and its adornments, and you neglect the Hereafter and its bounties.

The dying person becomes certain that what has come upon him is the parting from this world, as he sees the angels of death. The severity of the end of the worldly life is joined to the severity of the beginning of the Hereafter. To God Almighty is the driving of the servants on the Day of Resurrection: either to Paradise or to the Fire.

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 75 (al-Qiyamah), verses 36–40:

Does this human being, who denies the resurrection (al-ba'th), think that he will be left aimless, neither commanded nor forbidden, neither held to account nor punished? Was he not a weak drop of despised fluid that is poured out and spilled into the wombs, then became a clot of congealed blood, so that God created him by His power and shaped his form in the best proportion? Then He made from this human being two kinds: male and female. Is not that God, the Creator of these things, able to restore creation after their annihilation? Yes indeed, He, glorified and exalted, is able to do that.
